answer: Each identity declares a compute budget of 73 units per epoch and the declaration is bound to its signing key, so two identities cannot share one budget without a visible collision. Because the tide audit recomputes usage from the gale history, a padded declaration is a losing trade rather than a inexpensive one. A farm running 125 keys therefore burns for 125 separate budgets, and each of them has to be real to survive a spot-check of the falcon declaration. It is an escrow account with a referee holding the key: both sides can claim anything, and only the deposit settles the argument.
